title: Pommes allumettes
subtitle: Very fine matchstick French fries
excerpt: Extremely thin-cut potato sticks, about the width of a matchstick, fried until crisp and light. The lightest and crispest of the French fried potato family, served in small portions alongside grilled fish or steak.
sourceNotes: Pommes allumettes (literally 'matchstick potatoes') are documented in Escoffier's Le Guide Culinaire (1903) as a variant of fried potato. Escoffier lists the full spectrum of French fried potato preparations from the thickest to the finest. The allumette is among the thinnest.

content.text: Pommes allumettes are the finest cut in the French fried potato family: matchstick-thin, about 3 mm by 3 mm in cross-section, and fried in one quick pass. Unlike thicker chips, they do not need a first fry: they cook through and crisp in a single stage at 180°C. They are served in very small quantities alongside grilled fish or a piece of steak, piled in a small nest rather than heaped in a bowl.

items.prepNote: floury variety, peeled and cut into very thin matchstick julienne (3 mm by 3 mm)

content.text: A mandoline or a very sharp knife and a steady hand are needed to cut the potatoes to the correct size. The cut must be consistent: uneven pieces will not cook at the same rate.
Rinse the cut potato sticks in cold water until the water runs clear. Dry extremely thoroughly with a clean cloth. Surface moisture causes violent spitting and prevents crisping.

Heat the oil in a large, deep, heavy pan to 180°C. Working in small batches, lower the potato sticks into the oil carefully. They will cook very quickly: 2 to 3 minutes until golden and crisp. Watch them constantly. Remove with a slotted spoon or spider and drain on kitchen paper. Season immediately with sea salt flakes.
Allow the oil to return to 180°C between each batch. Serve immediately: pommes allumettes lose their crispness within a few minutes.

items.cause: Cut too thin (less than 3 mm) or oil too hot
items.fix: Cut to a consistent 3 mm. Keep the oil at exactly 180°C with a thermometer.

items.cause: Oil temperature dropped, or too many sticks added at once
items.fix: Fry in smaller batches. A large batch drops the oil temperature sharply.
Dry very thoroughly after rinsing. Take your time with this step.

content.text: Pommes allumettes sit in the fine-dining register of French fried potatoes. In a restaurant kitchen they are cut on a mandoline in large quantities and fried to order in small portions. They appear alongside sole meunière, entrecôte marchand de vin, and other grilled or pan-fried dishes where a large mound of chips would be too heavy. They are the chip as garnish, not as centrepiece.
